info.title: Blue REST API
info.description:
REST API for Blue. Authenticate with a Personal Access Token (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`) and scope requests with the `blue-org-id` header (the legacy `x-bloo-company-id` is still accepted). Every operation is available as RPC (`POST /v1/<operation>`); core resources also have resource-style routes.

**File uploads** use a presigned flow: `GET /uploads?filename=...` (same Bearer token, plus the `blue-workspace-id` header) returns `{ url, method: "PUT", headers, fields }`; PUT the binary to that URL, then finalize with `PUT /uploads/{uid}/confirm`. List uploaded files with `list-files`.

post.description: List the organizations (orgs) you belong to, with your access level in each. Use the returned id as the organizationId argument of other tools.

Read your authenticated identity and the selected organization, including your organization access level. Organization access does not imply a particular workspace role. Use list-organizations to choose an organization.

Start a workspace/database CSV, report CSV, chart-record CSV or template PDF export; then poll status with the returned kind and the same requestId for download links. Acceptance is not completion. Use a new requestId for a new export; retrying identical input reuses a retained receipt, while changed input is rejected. Export rate limits still apply to start/retry calls; status does not start another job. Receipts retain up to seven days and 10000 completed/failed requests per queue, so an evicted ID can start new work: do not retry an old unknown receipt blindly. NOT_FOUND means no retained receipt for this caller/organization/kind. Existing workers also email the requester. CSV links expire seven days after generation. PDF requires an active compatible template and has a 250-record cap. Report data follows creator permissions; chart record exports also enforce requester record/field access.

requestId.description: Caller-chosen retry ID; letters, digits, underscores and hyphens

post.description: Queue a workspace copy. Returns queued status, not a finished workspace ID. Use list-workspaces in the destination organization to find the named copy after the worker finishes; do not repeat the request. All supported include options default to true. fields controls copying generic databases and field definitions. Field sharing is preserved unless fieldSharing requests COPY for an eligible shared field. The API allows one active copy per user.

destinationOrganizationId.description: Destination organization ID or slug; defaults to the current organization

post.description: Archive a workspace or return an archived workspace to active use. Requires workspace owner/admin access. This does not delete the workspace or restore a deleted workspace. Archiving removes workspace folder placement.

archived.description: true to archive; false to unarchive

post.description: Change workspace metadata and settings. Requires workspace owner/admin access. Omitted settings stay unchanged. features replaces the complete feature configuration: read get-workspace first and preserve entries you need. Records are database menu items, not a workspace feature toggle.

description.description: HTML description; empty string clears it

post.description: Read workspace details, canonical app URL, archive state, your workspace access level, and feature settings before making changes.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: List workspaces the user has access to. Call this first — most other tools require a workspaceId. Returns id, name, slug, description, archived status, and canonical app URL.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Create a workspace in the current organization. For templates, call list-workspace-templates first and pass an item id as templateId. Blank creation returns the new workspace. Template creation runs in the background and may return status=queued; do not repeat the create request. Use list-workspaces to find the named workspace after the copy completes.

templateId.description: ID from list-workspace-templates; starts an asynchronous copy

folderId.description: Place the new workspace in this folder ID

post.description: List the workspace templates available to the caller. Each item's `id` is what create-workspace takes as `templateId`, so call this first when a workspace should start from a template. Defaults to the organization's own saved templates; pass official: true for Blue's public gallery. Templates that belong to a multi-workspace bundle are left out — a bundle can only be created whole, not one workspace at a time.

official.description: List Blue's public template gallery instead of the organization's own templates (default: false)

category.description: Only return templates in this category

post.description: Create a blank workspace, database/tab and up to 50 generic fields, or resume setup in an existing workspace. Lists/tags are SELECT_SINGLE/SELECT_MULTI fields with configuration.options [{id,title,color}]; assignees and dates are ordinary fields. Supply fresh stable IDs for database, view, tab, fields and options. On create, the new workspace's blank default database is renamed and reused, so the response returns its database/view/tab IDs instead of the supplied ones. Writes run sequentially and are not atomic. On PARTIAL, keep completed resources and resume with target.action=resume and the returned workspaceId using the SAME IDs/configuration. Existing matching fields are reused; mismatched definitions are refused. Creation has no workspace retry key: if workspaceId is null after an uncertain create, inspect list-workspaces before retrying. Templates use create-workspace separately, then resume after the copy finishes. This tool creates schema, not records or invitations.

List records (tasks/items) with filtering and pagination. Can filter by workspace, list, status, assignees, tags, or due date (window, presence, or overdue). Returns a summary view — use get-record for full details including checklists and custom fields.

workspaceId.description: Filter by workspace ID. If omitted, lists across all workspaces.

dueStart.description: Due-date window start (ISO date or datetime). Must be sent together with dueEnd. Matches records whose start/due span overlaps the window.

dueEnd.description: Due-date window end (ISO date or datetime). Must be sent together with dueStart.

hasDueDate.description: true → only records that have a due date; false → only records without one.

overdue.description: true → only records whose due date is in the past (all-day dates count once their day has ended). Combine with done:false for actionable overdue work.

post.description: Get full details and a canonical app URL for a single record by ID, including description, checklists, custom field values, tags, and assignees. Use list-records first to find record IDs.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Count records matching a filter. Useful for dashboards or checking how many tasks are open/done in a workspace without fetching full data. Can also count by due date (window, presence, or overdue).

dueStart.description: Due-date window start (ISO date or datetime). Must be sent together with dueEnd. Matches records whose start/due span overlaps the window.

dueEnd.description: Due-date window end (ISO date or datetime). Must be sent together with dueStart.

hasDueDate.description: true → only records that have a due date; false → only records without one.

overdue.description: true → only records whose due date is in the past (all-day dates count once their day has ended). Combine with done:false for actionable overdue work.

post.description: Create a new record (task/item) in a workspace. Requires a workspaceId from list-workspaces. Optionally place it in a specific list (use list-lists to get list IDs), assign users, and apply tags.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID to create the record in

listId.description: List ID to place the record in. If omitted, uses the first list.

description.description: Record description (plain text; blank lines become paragraphs, newlines become line breaks)

descriptionHtml.description: Record description as HTML. Sanitized server-side. Do not send with description.

startedAt.description: Start date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

duedAt.description: Due date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

allDay.description: Force the dates to be all-day (a floating calendar date shown identically in every timezone) or timed. Usually unnecessary: bare YYYY-MM-DD dates are all-day automatically.

post.description: Update fields on an existing record. Only provide the fields you want to change — omitted fields are left unchanged. Use move-record instead to change which list a record is in.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

description.description: New description (plain text; blank lines become paragraphs, newlines become line breaks)

descriptionHtml.description: New description as HTML. Sanitized server-side. Do not send with description.

done.description: Set the done status. Pass true to mark as done, false to mark as not done.

startedAt.description: Start date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

duedAt.description: Due date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

allDay.description: Force the dates to be all-day (a floating calendar date shown identically in every timezone) or timed. Usually unnecessary: bare YYYY-MM-DD dates are all-day automatically.

assigneeIds.description: User IDs to assign. Replaces all current assignees.

post.description: Move a record to a different list (column/status). Use list-lists to get available list IDs for the workspace.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

post.description: Permanently delete a record. This cannot be undone. The record is moved to trash internally but removed from the workspace. Use get-record first to verify you are deleting the correct record.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

post.description: Search for records by title within a workspace (does not match description/comment content). This is the right tool to find records in large workspaces — it queries the backend directly rather than filtering a loaded page, so it finds matches list-records would never page to. Returns a summary view including due dates; use get-record for full detail. Check pageInfo.hasNextPage and pass skip to page through results — a search can silently return only the first page otherwise.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID or slug to search within

query.description: Search text to match against record titles

archived.description: Archive scope: omit/false searches only active (non-archived) records; true searches ONLY archived records (not active + archived combined — there is no "both" option).

post.description: List all lists (columns/statuses) in a workspace. Lists represent workflow stages and contain records. Use this to get list IDs needed by create-record and move-record.
Create a new list (column/status) in a workspace. Lists represent workflow stages that contain records. Lists are ordered left-to-right; the response includes `rank`, the stable order key to sort by.
List tags available in a workspace. Use this to get tag IDs needed by create-record and set-tags-on-record.
Create a new tag in a workspace. Returns the tag ID, which can then be applied to records via create-record or set-tags-on-record.

color.description: Tag color (hex code). Defaults to a standard blue if omitted.

post.description: Set tags on a record. This replaces all existing tags — pass the complete list of tag IDs you want on the record. To add a tag without removing others, first get-record to see current tags, then include them all.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to set on the record

post.description: Remove a user’s membership from one workspace using the authorized membership-removal API. Requires workspace or organization OWNER/ADMIN; the workspace owner cannot be removed. Also removes their workspace record/checklist assignments, automation assignee targets and personal saved views, and revokes workspace inbox/inbound access. Organization membership and organization-admin access remain. Returns verified absence of workspace membership; an already absent membership is a no-op. A missing user or failed read is an error, not proof of removal.

Change an existing member to a built-in access level or a custom workspace role. Built-in assignment clears any custom role; a custom role uses MEMBER as its base level. Requires workspace or organization OWNER/ADMIN access. Cannot change yourself or the workspace owner, and cannot grant OWNER. Does not invite users. The API records activity and sends a role-change notification; non-admin organization membership can be reclassified from the member’s workspace levels. Returns verified membership after the write. Repeating an identical current assignment is a no-op.

List custom roles in one workspace, sorted by name, with role IDs and a permission summary. Use these IDs for roleId when inviting or updating workspace members. An empty list means no custom roles were returned; built-in OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER, CLIENT, COMMENT_ONLY and VIEW_ONLY access levels are separate from custom roles. This summary is not the full effective permission policy: database, field, view and conditional rules also apply.

List users in the company or a specific workspace. By default lists all company users. Pass workspaceId to list only members of that workspace — useful for knowing who can be assigned to records. Includes organizationAccessLevel, workspaceAccessLevel and workspaceRole (custom role ID/name). Workspace fields are null for organization-only results; these are membership settings, not a complete effective permission evaluation.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID or slug to list only members of that workspace. Omit to list all company users.

search.description: Search by first or last name (does not match email)

post.description: Add or invite a person to a workspace by email. Someone who is already in the organization joins the workspace immediately; anyone else is emailed an invitation that expires in seven days. Requires OWNER, ADMIN, MEMBER or CLIENT access in the target workspace, or OWNER/ADMIN in the organization — view-only and comment-only members cannot invite. You cannot grant an access level above your own: an ADMIN cannot make someone an OWNER, a MEMBER cannot make someone an ADMIN, and a CLIENT can only invite other CLIENTs. An organization OWNER always joins a workspace as ADMIN whatever level you ask for.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID or slug to add the person to

email.description: Email address of the person to add or invite

accessLevel.description: Access level to request in the workspace. Cannot be higher than your own level. Organization owners join as ADMIN, and resending an existing invitation keeps its stored level.

roleId.description: Optional custom role ID to assign. Must belong to this workspace.

post.description: List custom fields defined in a workspace. Returns field names, types (text, number, dropdown, checkbox, etc.), and available options. Custom field values for a specific record are returned by get-record.

Set a custom field value on a record. Use list-custom-fields to find the field ID and type, then pass the appropriate value parameter for that type. Only provide the value parameters that match the field type. For a Long text field, pass html to preserve rich-text formatting — passing only text clears any existing formatting.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

text.description: Value for text, email, URL, or phone fields

html.description: Rich-text HTML value for Long text fields — preserves formatting. Takes precedence over text when both are set.

number.description: Value for number or currency fields

customFieldOptionId.description: Option ID for single-select dropdown fields

customFieldOptionIds.description: Option IDs for multi-select dropdown fields

startDate.description: Start date for date range fields (ISO 8601)

endDate.description: End date for date range fields (ISO 8601)

granularity.description: For date range fields: whether the date is a floating all-day date or a precise instant. A bare UTC-midnight startDate/endDate without this is inferred as ALL_DAY — pass TIMED explicitly if you mean a real midnight-UTC instant.

tableRows.description: Rows for a Table field; each is { cells: { <columnId>: value } }. Get column IDs from list-custom-fields tableColumns. Replaces all existing rows.

post.description: Delete one checklist item, preserving its checklist and other items. Use get-record to find the item ID. This tool cannot undo deletion.

Rename or reorder a checklist with action=update, or remove it and its items with action=delete. Use get-record to discover checklist IDs and positions. Update changes only supplied properties; position=0 is valid. For creation use create-checklist. This tool cannot undo deletion.

Create a new checklist on a record. A record can have multiple checklists. Supply workspaceId for records without a list; this avoids the legacy list-based workspace lookup. After creating, use create-checklist-item to add items to it.

workspaceId.description: Workspace containing the record; required for records without a list

recordId.description: The record ID to add the checklist to

post.description: Add an item to an existing checklist. Requires a checklistId from create-checklist or get-record. Supply workspaceId for records without a list.

workspaceId.description: Workspace containing the checklist; required for records without a list

post.description: Update a checklist item: toggle completion, rename, reorder, or move to another checklist with checklistId. Only supplied fields change. Moving requires permission on both source and destination. Supply workspaceId for records without a list.

workspaceId.description: Source workspace; required for records without a list

checklistId.description: Destination checklist ID when moving the item

post.description: Delete a comment within your comment-delete permissions. Clears its body and removes attachments; the activity stream can retain a deleted-comment marker. This tool cannot restore the comment.

Replace a comment body within your comment-edit permissions. Plain-text line breaks are preserved. Optional HTML takes precedence and is sanitized by the API; its plain-text mirror is derived from the HTML. Use delete-comment to remove a comment instead of replacing it with an empty body.

html.description: Optional replacement HTML, taking precedence over text

post.description: Add a comment to a record. Comments are visible to all workspace members. Blank lines in text become paragraphs and single newlines become line breaks. Pass html instead for rich formatting such as bold, lists or links.

recordId.description: The record ID to comment on

text.description: Comment text (plain text; line breaks are preserved)

html.description: Comment body as HTML, for rich formatting. Sanitized server-side. Takes precedence over text — the comment’s stored plain-text mirror (used for search) is derived from this HTML, not from text.

post.description: Read the activity feed — who did what, when — across the whole company or a single workspace. Omit workspaceId for company-wide activity. Use this to understand recent changes, audit actions, or catch up on a workspace. Newest first.

workspaceId.description: Scope to one workspace. Omit for company-wide activity.

userId.description: Filter to activity by a specific user ID

categories.description: Filter by activity categories (e.g. CREATE_TODO, CREATE_COMMENT, COMPLETE_TODO). Omit for all.

after.description: Pagination cursor (endCursor from a previous call)

post.description: Read the full history of a single record — its comments and its actions (field changes, moves, assignments, status changes). Use this to understand how a record reached its current state.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

type.description: Filter to comments only, actions only, or all (default: all)

post.description: List the pages in a workspace with canonical app URLs (titles and metadata, no body). Use get-document for the full HTML content.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Get a single page including its full HTML content and canonical app URL. Use list-documents to find IDs.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the document belongs to (recommended for scoping)

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Create, update, move, or delete a document page. Pages form a tree: parentId nests a page under another, position orders siblings. create requires workspaceId; update, move, and delete require documentId. Content is HTML. On update, content replaces the whole body; an empty string clears it, and omitting it leaves it unchanged. icon sets/clears the page icon (create/update). Deleting a page moves it AND its subpages to trash.

documentId.description: Document ID (required for update, move, and delete)

content.description: Complete HTML body; on update, an empty string clears it and omission leaves it unchanged

parentId.description: Parent page ID (create/move); null moves the page to the root level

icon.description: Lucide icon name from the curated docs icon set (create/update); null clears it

post.description: List the saved views (saved record filters/layouts) in a workspace. Use get-saved-view to read a view's full configuration.

databaseId.description: Scope saved views to this record database

post.description: Get a single saved view including its viewConfig — the filter, sort, and grouping configuration. Inspect this to understand or reproduce how a team slices their records.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the view belongs to (recommended for scoping)

post.description: Create, edit, duplicate, position or delete a saved record view in an explicit workspace/database. Omitted edit settings remain unchanged; supplied viewConfig replaces the whole configuration (use get-saved-view first). To change layout on edit, include viewType in viewConfig. Use generic field IDs in filters and layout configuration. Shared views require the API sharing permission. Duplicate creates a personal copy unless isShared is explicitly true. Create and duplicate have no retry key: inspect list-saved-views after an uncertain response before retrying. Delete clears defaults and favorites. Position is a numeric menu position, not a zero-based index.

Create, update, or delete a dependency between two records. type is from the perspective of recordId: BLOCKED_BY means recordId is blocked by otherRecordId; BLOCKING means recordId blocks otherRecordId. update changes an existing edge's type; delete removes the edge.

otherRecordId.description: The other record (todo) ID in the relationship

type.description: Dependency type. Required for create/update; defaults to BLOCKED_BY on create.

post.description: Replace the complete list of direct report recipients with VIEWER or EDITOR access. EDITOR can also manage direct sharing. Read get-report first to preserve existing recipients. users=[] clears direct shares; creator, organization-admin and inherited folder access remain. Recipients must belong to the organization. Report data is evaluated with the creator’s permissions, so recipients can see the creator-authorized report data. Only callers authorized to manage report access can write. This replaces the list atomically but has no version check; concurrent sharing edits can overwrite each other. Does not change sources or report content.

Read server-calculated sum, average, minimum, maximum, and count for up to 20 report fields. Use field IDs from list-database-fields. Report sources, filters and creator permissions determine the data scope; report sharing determines access. An additional filter narrows the report. Totals may use the report aggregation cache.

field.description: Field ID or a report field key

originalIds.description: Underlying field IDs for a merged report field

filter.description: Additional TodosFilter; organization scope is enforced by the tool

post.description: List reports in the company, including their canonical app URLs. Reports aggregate records across one or more workspaces. Use get-report for a report's full config and get-report-data for its records.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Get a single report including its full config, data sources (workspaces + filters), members, owning organization, and canonical app URL.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Get the records a report resolves to, plus the total count. The report's own data sources and filters apply; pass an optional additional filter to narrow further.

filter.description: Optional additional TodosFilter (e.g. { "done": false }) applied on top of the report

post.description: Create, update, delete, duplicate, or refresh a report. Create requires title; other actions require reportId. dataSources replaces ALL sources on update; omitted sources and config remain unchanged. Duplicate copies configuration and sources, makes you the creator, and does not copy sharing. Refresh invalidates aggregation caches; results are computed on the next read.

workspaceIds.description: Workspace IDs to include as the report's data source (create only)

filter.description: Optional TodosFilter for the data source (create only)

dataSources.description: Create/update: complete replacement of sources; [] removes all sources. Cannot combine with top-level workspaceIds/filter. Source IDs are regenerated.

workspaceIds.description: Omitted or empty means ALL workspaces accessible to the report creator

filter.description: TodosFilter; omit or use {} for no filter

config.description: Update only: complete report display configuration; {} resets it

post.description: Edit a chart or move it to another editable dashboard. Omitted top-level settings remain unchanged. metadata replaces the chart configuration: use get-chart first and retain query/presentation settings you need. Send width and height together, or both null to reset sizing. Calculation may continue in the background.

dashboardId.description: Destination dashboard ID when moving a chart

filter.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

filters.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

post.description: Save a grouped or manual formula chart in an editable dashboard. Use preview-chart to check its numbers first. Calculation can continue in the background; read get-chart until calculation finishes. Creation is not idempotent: after an uncertain timeout, inspect list-charts before retrying.

dashboardId.description: Target dashboard ID; you must be able to edit it

type.description: BAR/PIE for grouped charts; STAT for manual formula cards

metadata.description: Grouped query and/or presentation. Field IDs bind fields without relying on names.

filter.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

filters.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

chartSegments.description: Manual formula segments; use these or metadata.query, not both

filter.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

post.description: Calculate a proposed grouped or manual formula chart without saving it. Requires dashboard edit access. Scope metadata.query.filters.projectIds to the intended workspaces. For a record count, omit the metric field binding. Preview IDs are temporary and cannot be used to edit saved charts.

dashboardId.description: Target dashboard ID; you must be able to edit it

type.description: BAR/PIE for grouped charts; STAT for manual formula cards

metadata.description: Grouped query and/or presentation. Field IDs bind fields without relying on names.

filter.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

filters.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

chartSegments.description: Manual formula segments; use these or metadata.query, not both

filter.description: TodoFilterInput; use projectIds to scope workspaces

post.description: Read chart configuration, grouping, metrics, filters, presentation, and stored results before editing. Results may be stale while isCalculating or needCalculation is true; isOverBudget means calculation exceeded its budget. Formula details follow your dashboard permissions.
List the charts in a dashboard, including each chart's computed segment values. Use this to read dashboard metrics (stats, bar/pie breakdowns).
Delete a chart, or trigger recalculation of one or more charts (refresh their values after underlying records change). delete requires chartId; recalculate requires chartIds.

chartIds.description: Chart IDs to recalculate (required for recalculate)

post.description: Replace all direct dashboard recipients (VIEWER or EDITOR), change the creator-only allowViewerChartData setting, or both. Omitted settings are preserved. Read get-dashboard before replacing recipients; users=[] clears direct grants but creator, organization-admin and folder access remain. EDITOR includes management of direct sharing. Recipients must belong to the organization. allowViewerChartData controls whether VIEWERs may open chart records; record and field access checks still apply. Changes have no version check, so concurrent recipient replacements can overwrite each other. Does not change charts or title.
List dashboards in the company with canonical app URLs, optionally scoped to a workspace. Use list-charts with a dashboard ID to read its charts and values.

workspaceId.description: Filter to dashboards scoped to this workspace

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Get a single dashboard's metadata (title, owner, members), owning organization, and canonical app URL. Use list-charts for its charts.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Create, update, or delete a dashboard. create requires title (optionally scope to a workspace); update requires dashboardId and title; delete requires dashboardId and removes the dashboard and all its charts.

title.description: Dashboard title (required for create and update)

workspaceId.description: Scope the dashboard to a workspace (create only)

dashboardId.description: Dashboard ID (required for update and delete)

post.description: Create, update, or delete a custom field DEFINITION in a workspace. (To read fields use list-custom-fields; to set a field value on a record use set-custom-field-value. For SELECT field options use manage-custom-field-options.) create requires workspaceId, name, and type; update and delete require customFieldId. Creating a TABLE field also requires columns.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID (required for create; recommended for update/delete scoping)

customFieldId.description: Custom field ID (required for update and delete)

type.description: Field type (required for create), e.g. TEXT_SINGLE, TEXT_MULTI, NUMBER, CURRENCY, PERCENT, DATE, SELECT_SINGLE, SELECT_MULTI, CHECKBOX, RATING, EMAIL, PHONE, URL, LOCATION, COUNTRY, FILE, TABLE

columns.description: Column definitions (required when type is "TABLE", 1-10 entries). Each column needs at least {name, type} where type is one of TEXT, NUMBER, DATE, CHECKBOX, SELECT_SINGLE, SELECT_MULTI, CURRENCY, FORMULA. SELECT_SINGLE/SELECT_MULTI need an options array of {label}.

post.description: Add or remove options (choices) on a SELECT_SINGLE / SELECT_MULTI custom field. add appends one or more options; remove deletes one option by ID.

options.description: Options to add (required for add), each { title, color? }

optionId.description: Option ID to remove (required for remove)

post.description: Read the value-change history of one field on a record. Pass `asOf` to get the value at a point in time instead of the full list. `field` is either a custom field ID or one of the default-field keys: $list, $completed, $due, $assignees.

field.description: Custom field ID, or a default-field key: $list, $completed, $due, $assignees

asOf.description: Return the single interval covering this instant instead of the full history list

before.description: Page backward: only intervals that opened before this instant

take.description: Max intervals to return (default 50), ignored with asOf

post.description: Read the re-bucketed time series for a saved field-value-history metric (see fieldMetrics for the list of metrics in a workspace, and createFieldMetric to define one).
List the public/embedded forms in a workspace with canonical editor URLs.

sort.description: Sort order, e.g. updatedAt_DESC (default) or title_ASC

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Get a single form including its canonical editor URL, full configuration and fields (with custom-field links).

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the form belongs to

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Create, update, delete, or duplicate a form. create requires workspaceId and title and configures the form in one call. update requires formId. All operations require workspaceId. Duplicate requires formId and accepts an optional title and destinationWorkspaceId. The API creates an active copy with branding shown; same-workspace copies retain the database, cross-workspace copies use the destination workspace original database. Use databaseId when creating or updating a form on a new database. Add/edit form FIELDS with manage-form-field after the form exists.

formId.description: Form ID (required for update, delete and duplicate)

title.description: Form title (required for create; optional for duplicate)

destinationWorkspaceId.description: Duplicate only; defaults to workspaceId (the source workspace)

databaseId.description: Create/update: submission database; null selects the workspace original database

redirectUrl.description: URL to redirect to after submit

listId.description: List ID that submissions land in

assigneeIds.description: User IDs to assign to new records

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to apply to new records

post.description: Add, update, or delete a field on a form. For upsert: omit formFieldId to add a new field, or pass an existing formFieldId to edit it. upsert requires workspaceId. field is one of title, description, tags, assignees, startedAt, duedAt, custom; only custom carries a customFieldId. delete requires formFieldId.

formFieldId.description: Form field ID — omit to add a new field, provide to edit; required for delete

customFieldId.description: Custom field ID (only when field is "custom")

name.description: Field label shown on the form

hidden.description: Whether the field is hidden (defaults to false)

addToDescription.description: Render the value into the record description

post.description: Edit an automation within its existing workspace and database. Omitted top-level settings are preserved. Supplying actions replaces the whole ordered action list; at least one action is required. Trigger settings follow API patch semantics: use explicit empty arrays/null to clear supported filters, and send the full desired generic binding when changing it. Omit trigger to keep it unchanged. name="" clears the label; groupId=null ungroups; isActive=false disables; position=0 is valid. Database ownership cannot be changed. Read get-automation before editing. Editing an active rule changes future execution immediately.

anyOf.description: Stable generic field ID from list-database-fields; use for lists, tags, assignees and dates too
Required for CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED. empty=false without optionIds means Any.
Generic records filter, evaluated after the triggering change

fieldId.description: Stable generic writable field ID; ADD_CUSTOM_FIELD sets its value and REMOVE_CUSTOM_FIELD removes it

optionIds.description: Option/user/reference record IDs for multi-value fields

metadata.description: Typed value or action settings; numeric writes use {number}, text writes {text}, dates {date} or {dateRule}

post.description: Create an ACTIVE automation in an explicit workspace and database. Trigger and actions use stable generic field IDs, including lists, tags, assignees and dates. Actions run in submitted order. CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED requires transition.from/to; ADD_CUSTOM_FIELD with fieldId and metadata sets a generic value. The API validates field mounts, permissions and cycles. Creation has no retry key: after a lost response, inspect list-automations before retrying to avoid duplicate rules. Use manage-automation to disable a rule.

fieldId.description: Stable generic field ID from list-database-fields; use for lists, tags, assignees and dates too

transition.description: Required for CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED. empty=false without optionIds means Any.

onlyIf.description: Generic records filter, evaluated after the triggering change

fieldId.description: Stable generic writable field ID; ADD_CUSTOM_FIELD sets its value and REMOVE_CUSTOM_FIELD removes it

optionIds.description: Option/user/reference record IDs for multi-value fields

metadata.description: Typed value or action settings; numeric writes use {number}, text writes {text}, dates {date} or {dateRule}

post.description: Read one automation in an explicit workspace: database binding, enabled state, trigger filters and schedule, generic field bindings, action configuration and needsAttention. Actions include their execution position. Legacy trigger record references are capped at 500 by the API. HTTP configuration may contain credentials; treat the response as sensitive. Use list-automations to discover IDs.
List the automations in a workspace, summarizing each one's trigger and actions. Use this to audit what automated behavior a workspace has configured.

customFieldIds.description: Only automations whose trigger references one of these custom field IDs. When set, skip/limit are ignored and every match is returned.

post.description: Enable, disable, rename, move (to a group), duplicate, or delete an automation. Duplicate requires destination workspaceId and databaseId, creates an inactive rule, and needs manage access to both source and destination. Generic bound fields must be mounted in the destination. Same-workspace copies retain the group; cross-workspace copies are ungrouped. Creation has no retry key: inspect list-automations after an uncertain response before retrying. Use create-automation to define a new rule and get-automation to inspect its full configuration.

name.description: Name for rename or duplicate. Empty string clears the name; omitted duplicate name uses the API copy default.

groupId.description: Target automation group ID (for move). null moves the automation to Ungrouped.

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID for scoping; required destination workspace for duplicate

databaseId.description: Required destination database for duplicate only

post.description: List the webhooks configured for the account.
Get a single webhook including its metadata. The signing secret is only ever returned once, in the create response — it cannot be retrieved later, including through this tool.

Discover events, create, update, disable, or delete a webhook. list-events is read-only and returns the server subscription event names. Use those exact names in events; delivered payload names may differ for MODERN-vocabulary webhooks. create requires url; update/disable/delete require webhookId. Re-enable a disabled webhook with update + enabled: true.

events.description: Exact subscription names returned by action list-events. Omit/empty to receive all events on create; omit to preserve events on update.

workspaceIds.description: Restrict the webhook to these workspace IDs (omit for all)

post.description: Attach a pull request from the workspace linked repository, or remove a PR/branch/commit link from a record. Requires the record database to disambiguate shared records. Attach accepts a PR number, #number or GitHub pull request URL; repeated attach pins the same link manually. The GitHub App installation and repository link must already exist. If workspace linkbacks are enabled, attach can post a GitHub comment. Detach removes only the Blue link, does not close a PR or delete a branch, and automatic discovery may recreate it. This tool does not configure issue mirroring.
Get the organization GitHub App installation status, and optionally a workspace repository link (which repo the workspace is connected to and whether it is active).

workspaceId.description: Workspace ID to include its repository link

post.description: List the GitHub pull requests, branches, and commits linked to a record, including live state (PR state, CI checks, review verdicts) from the stateCache field.

Set generic field values on up to 25 records in one database, at most 100 field writes total. Each field write is atomic; the batch and multi-field record updates are not. Processing continues after errors and rejections. Lists, tags, assignees, dates and other editable values use field IDs. Select and assignee values replace the whole set. Reuse batchId, entitySequence and the same values to retry safely. Use a NEW batchId when changing any values. entitySequence must be greater than earlier writes to each record/field, e.g. the current Unix time in milliseconds. Only ACCEPTED and REPLAYED are successes; inspect each outcome for conflicts and retryable failures.

batchId.description: Caller-supplied unique retry key for this exact batch

post.description: Create up to 25 records in one explicit database, sequentially, with one atomic API call per record. The batch is not atomic: errors are returned per item and later items still run. Supply a fresh random recordId (lowercase letter followed by 23 lowercase letters/digits) for each new record. Retry with the same IDs and payloads after partial failure or a lost response; existing records are not overwritten. An existing accessible record ID can join this database instead of creating a record. Use fieldValues with field IDs for lists, tags, assignees, dates and other fields; discover definitions with list-database-fields. An error can follow a committed write, so never generate a new ID merely to retry.

fieldValues.description: Generic writes: {fieldId,kind,value}; same shapes as set-database-field-value

post.description: Rename, move, share or delete one visible confirmed workspace file. Rename preserves its extension. Move requires a FILE folder in the same workspace; folderId=null moves to the root. shared=true enables its public share link. shared=false revokes direct sharing but a shared parent folder may still grant public access. Delete moves metadata to Trash and schedules byte cleanup; it is not an archive. Does not edit upload status or attach files to records; use generic file fields for attachments.

Confirm a file after sending raw bytes to the PUT URL returned by prepare-file-upload. Verifies object presence and declared size, updates workspace files and schedules supported image/PDF renditions. Safe to retry with the same uid; alreadyConfirmed reports a prior confirmation. Does not attach the file to a record. Workspace access and file permissions are required on every call.

Reserve storage and create a PENDING workspace file. Returns a short-lived PUT URL, required headers, fileId and uid. Send raw file bytes directly to that URL using the returned headers, then call complete-file-upload with uid. The declared size is bytes; plan limits still apply. This call does not transfer bytes or attach the file to a record. Every call creates a new pending file, so preserve its identifiers and do not repeat merely because the byte transfer failed. Unfinished uploads are reconciled after URL expiry.

Get metadata for one visible uploaded workspace file by its exact file ID. Returns attachment, folder, field and uploader details using file-list visibility checks. Pending uploads and export artifacts are excluded. Does not download binary content.

List files uploaded in a workspace (metadata: name, size, type, which record/folder, uploader). Filter by name, folder, or record. Record scope includes direct attachments, field files and comment attachments. Filters combine with AND. Omit folderId for every folder; null selects files outside folders. Binary content is not returned.

recordId.description: Only files attached to this record

folderId.description: Exact folder ID; null for files outside folders

post.description: Create, edit, move or delete a FILE folder in a workspace. Existing and parent folders must belong to that workspace. Moving uses an explicit parent ID or null for the root. Delete removes the folder, descendants and their files. Setting shared=true publishes the folder subtree through its share link. Organization workspace folders and analytics folders are separate.

operation.description: create: title, optional parentId; update: folderId and title/color/shared; move: folderId and parentId (null for root); delete: folderId

post.description: List accessible file folders in a workspace, or workspace folders in the current organization. FILE requires workspaceId. For FILE, omit parentId for all levels, pass null for root folders, or an ID for direct children. PROJECT lists organization workspace folders and does not accept workspaceId or parentId. Analytics folders are separate.

type.description: FILE for uploaded files; PROJECT for workspace organization

post.description: List every database in a workspace with its canonical app URL. A workspace can have more than one database (a CRM database, a bug tracker, and a task list can all live side by side) -- use this before list-database-fields, list-database-records, or create-database-record to find the databaseId you need. Every workspace has at least one database.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: List the views on a workspace tab rail: each entry names its view id, kind (table, board, calendar, timeline, or map -- absent for a plain table view), and which database it shows.

Replace a generic field definition configuration, preserving its type and stored record values. Read the current configuration with list-database-fields and supply the complete replacement, not a patch. Pass null to reset configuration where that field type permits it. Shared fields change in every database mounting them. Supported by the API: NUMBER, DATE, URL, SELECT_SINGLE, SELECT_MULTI, REFERENCE, REFERENCED_BY, LOOKUP, ROLLUP, TIME_IN_VALUE, UNIQUE_ID, TIME_DURATION. The API validates settings, dependencies and existing values; unsupported types and unsafe changes are rejected. Use manage-database-field-option for option definitions, rename-database-field for the name, and set-database-field-value for record values.

configuration.description: Complete type-specific configuration object, or explicit null to reset

post.description: List fields mounted on a database with their types and configuration. Set forView=true to discover fields visible to the caller and their selectable options (returned in options, not configuration). The default schema-editor projection requires field-management access and may omit options. Use the returned IDs with create-database-record, set-database-field-value, and manage-database-field-option.

forView.description: Read visible fields and option choices instead of the schema-editor projection

post.description: Define a new field and mount it on a database in one step. Supported types: TEXT_SINGLE, TEXT_MULTI, NUMBER, PERCENT, RATING, CURRENCY, CHECKBOX, SELECT_SINGLE, SELECT_MULTI, DATE, DATE_RANGE, ASSIGNEE, REFERENCE, FILE, EMAIL, URL, PHONE, COUNTRY, LOCATION. For SELECT_SINGLE/SELECT_MULTI, create the field first, then create choices with manage-database-field-option. configuration.options is not supported: it does not create selectable options. Use the returned option IDs with set-database-field-value. For workspace setup with initial fields and options, use bootstrap-workspace.

databaseId.description: The database to mount the new field on

fieldId.description: A unique id you choose for the new field (e.g. a UUID). Also makes a retry idempotent.

type.description: The field type, e.g. TEXT_SINGLE, NUMBER, SELECT_SINGLE, DATE, CHECKBOX

configuration.description: Type-specific settings. Create select options separately with manage-database-field-option.

post.description: Rename an existing field. Its type and configuration are unchanged.
Permanently retire a field and its stored values. Refused while a database still designates it (e.g. as its display field) or another live field still depends on it.

Share an existing field onto another database by mounting it there. Idempotent -- a field already on the database keeps its rank. The field, and any values already stored for records that live in both databases, become visible on the new database.

databaseId.description: The database to mount the field on

fieldId.description: The field ID to mount (from list-database-fields on another database)

post.description: Stop sharing a field with one database by unmounting it. Stored values are never destroyed -- they reappear if the field is mounted again, or on any other database it is still mounted on.

databaseId.description: The database to unmount the field from

post.description: Create, update, reorder, or delete an option on a generic select field, including fields used as lists or tags. Find field and option IDs with list-database-fields(forView=true); never infer them from field names. Options belong to the shared field: changes affect every database mounting it. Create uses a caller-chosen optionId for safe retries; an existing ID is not updated. Delete retires the option and rewrites all stored selections: supply a replacement optionId from the same field, or explicitly pass null to clear those selections. This can also remove automation links to the retired option. To change a record selection, use set-database-field-value instead.

optionId.description: Existing option ID, or a new caller-chosen UUID for create

recordScope.description: Optional record scope when adding from a picker with field edit access

clientMutationId.description: Unique idempotency key; reuse it when retrying the same deletion

replacementOptionId.description: Required: live option ID on this field, or null to clear affected selections

post.description: Archive or unarchive a record in one explicit database. Set archived=false to restore it to active records; this does not restore a deleted record from Trash. Other database memberships remain unchanged. Supply a unique clientMutationId and increasing entitySequence for this record/database archive lane. Retry the identical request with the same ID and sequence. ACCEPTED/REPLAYED confirms receipt acceptance; other outcomes are refusals or retry states. A replay returns the original receipt and does not override a later change. Use list-database-records with includeArchived=true to inspect current membership state.

Duplicate a record within an explicit database, copying supported mounted field values, checklists and comments. Works on generic databases without lists. Supply a fresh random destinationRecordId (lowercase letter followed by 23 lowercase letters/digits). The copy uses multiple transactions and can partially complete. Retry the SAME source, database and destination ID after a failure; never generate another ID merely to retry. Do not reuse an unrelated existing record ID: the API can write copied values onto that record. copiedFieldIds reports fields written by this call, so it may be empty on a successful retry. Derived values follow the backend copy rules.

destinationRecordId.description: Fresh caller-supplied ID; preserve it for retries

post.description: List the records in one database, with a canonical app URL and every mounted field's current value. Use list-database-fields first to know what each field id means. Paginate with the returned nextCursor as the next call's cursor.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous call's nextCursor

includeArchived.description: Include records archived in this database (default false)

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.description: Create a record in an explicit database. Unlike create-record, this works on any database -- including one with no lists at all -- and never guesses which database to use. Pass fieldValues (each { fieldId, kind, value }, kinds matching a field's type: "text" -> {text} or {html}, "number" -> {number}, "checkbox" -> boolean, "select" -> [optionId], "date" -> {start, end, timezone, granularity}, "assignee"/"reference" -> [id, ...]) to set other fields at creation time. If the database has a required creation form, missing required fields are rejected.

title.description: The record's display value (the database's display field)

groupOptionId.description: A live option id on the database's grouping field (board column / list), if it has one

fieldValues.description: Other field values to set at creation, each { fieldId, kind, value }

post.description: Optional operation=add/remove applies atomic membership deltas for select (SELECT_MULTI) or assignee fields; value is an ID array. Unrelated members remain. Assignee eligibility and single-assignee rules still apply. Use the same operation, IDs, mutation ID and sequence on retry. Default operation=set keeps whole-value replacement. Set one field's value on an existing record, generically -- works for any mounted field, not just legacy custom fields. `kind` must match the field's type: "text" -> {text} or {html}, "number" -> {number, currency?}, "checkbox" -> a boolean, "select" -> an array of option ids (whole-set replace), "date" -> {start, end, timezone?, granularity?}, "assignee"/"reference"/"file" -> an array of ids, "country" -> an array of country codes, "contact" -> {text, regionCode?}, "location" -> {text, latitude, longitude}. Use list-database-fields to find the fieldId and its type. Pass your own clientMutationId (any unique string) so a retry is safe, and a monotonically increasing entitySequence (e.g. the current Unix time in milliseconds) -- a lower one than a previous call on the same record+field is refused as a conflict.

operation.description: Default set replaces the value. Add/remove atomically change SELECT_MULTI options or ASSIGNEE users; value is an array of IDs.

databaseId.description: The database the record lives in

kind.description: The write kind matching the field's type, e.g. text, number, checkbox, select, date

value.description: The value, shaped as the kind's own doc line above describes

clientMutationId.description: Your own idempotency key for this write

entitySequence.description: A number greater than any you have sent before for this record+field, e.g. Date.now()

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID to create the record in

listId.description: List ID to place the record in. If omitted, uses the first list.

description.description: Record description (plain text; blank lines become paragraphs, newlines become line breaks)

descriptionHtml.description: Record description as HTML. Sanitized server-side. Do not send with description.

startedAt.description: Start date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

duedAt.description: Due date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

allDay.description: Force the dates to be all-day (a floating calendar date shown identically in every timezone) or timed. Usually unnecessary: bare YYYY-MM-DD dates are all-day automatically.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

description.description: New description (plain text; blank lines become paragraphs, newlines become line breaks)

descriptionHtml.description: New description as HTML. Sanitized server-side. Do not send with description.

done.description: Set the done status. Pass true to mark as done, false to mark as not done.

startedAt.description: Start date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

duedAt.description: Due date. Send a bare YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day date, or ISO 8601 for a timed one.

allDay.description: Force the dates to be all-day (a floating calendar date shown identically in every timezone) or timed. Usually unnecessary: bare YYYY-MM-DD dates are all-day automatically.

assigneeIds.description: User IDs to assign. Replaces all current assignees.

post.summary: Move a record to another list

workspaceId.description: The workspace ID the record belongs to

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

templateId.description: ID from list-workspace-templates; starts an asynchronous copy

folderId.description: Place the new workspace in this folder ID

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.summary: Create a field on a table

databaseId.description: The database to mount the new field on

fieldId.description: A unique id you choose for the new field (e.g. a UUID). Also makes a retry idempotent.

type.description: The field type, e.g. TEXT_SINGLE, NUMBER, SELECT_SINGLE, DATE, CHECKBOX

configuration.description: Type-specific settings. Create select options separately with manage-database-field-option.

url.description: Canonical app link. Requires normal app access; not a public sharing link.

post.summary: Create a record in a table

title.description: The record's display value (the database's display field)

groupOptionId.description: A live option id on the database's grouping field (board column / list), if it has one

fieldValues.description: Other field values to set at creation, each { fieldId, kind, value }

patch.summary: Set a field value on a record

operation.description: Default set replaces the value. Add/remove atomically change SELECT_MULTI options or ASSIGNEE users; value is an array of IDs.

databaseId.description: The database the record lives in

kind.description: The write kind matching the field's type, e.g. text, number, checkbox, select, date

value.description: The value, shaped as the kind's own doc line above describes

clientMutationId.description: Your own idempotency key for this write

entitySequence.description: A number greater than any you have sent before for this record+field, e.g. Date.now()
